opex.name: Operating expenses
opex.note: Research, engineering and running the business side of the fabs — shown as one line, including other operating income, net.

follow100Note: Of every $100 of revenue, $36.80 stayed as profit; high-performance computing alone brought in $52 of it, and advanced 7nm-and-below nodes were 67% of wafer revenue.
footerNote: TSMC reports in New Taiwan dollars (revenue NT$673.5B; net income attributable to shareholders NT$247.8B). Dollar figures are converted at NT$32.35 per US$1 — implied by TSMC's own stated US-dollar revenue of $20.82B (NT$ revenue divided by that figure). Operating expenses are shown as one line combining operating expenses with other operating income, net, as in TSMC's earnings release. Segment dollars are the platform shares of revenue from TSMC's official Q2 2024 materials applied to revenue. The tax line is set so the flow lands on net income attributable to TSMC shareholders.
otherDetail: Non-operating income of NT$19.8B (about $0.6B) — mostly NT$21.0B of interest earned on TSMC's large cash pile, plus a NT$2.2B foreign-exchange gain and NT$1.2B from associates, partly offset by NT$2.6B of finance costs and NT$2.1B of other losses.

sources.label: Official earnings release with Q3 guidance (SEC EDGAR)

takeaways.text: High-performance computing passed half of revenue for the first time, jumping 28% in one quarter on demand for AI accelerators, while smartphone chip sales slipped 1% in their seasonal lull.
takeaways.title: AI chips are now the majority

takeaways.text: A 53.2% gross margin and 42.5% operating margin — 3nm and 5nm together were half of wafer revenue, and advanced nodes (7nm and beyond) were 67%.
takeaways.title: Margins held above 53%

takeaways.text: Management guided third-quarter revenue to $22.4–23.2B with a gross margin of 53.5–55.5%, expecting strong smartphone and AI-related demand for its leading-edge technologies.
takeaways.title: A bigger Q3 guided

verdict: TSMC's revenue rose 40% to NT$673.5B ($20.8B) as strong demand for its 3nm and 5nm chips outweighed soft smartphone season — and with a 53.2% gross margin, it kept NT$247.8B ($7.7B) as profit, up 36%.
